sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1,702.2 million in FY2016 to $12,001.3 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a step change, not a smooth ramp: growth ran 46.2% in FY2017 and 49.1% in FY2020, then slowed to 8.9% in FY2025 [D41][D194][D446].
The FY2020 step came from the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO in the E.U. in the third quarter of 2020 [P51].
FY2024 broke the trend, with operating margin at -2.1% on $4.6 billion of AIPR&D, including $4.4 billion for Alpine [F34][P11].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO reached $10,312.7 million, or 85.9% of revenue, in FY2025 [S45][D529].
Its contribution to growth fell to 0.7pp in FY2025 from 26.3pp in FY2022, while ALYFTREK added 7.6pp in its first year [D531][D522][D590].
Net product revenues rose $950.5 million, or 9%, in FY2025 on continued demand [P3].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 95.6% CAGR against 24.2% [F197][F196].
Diluted EPS rose to $15.32 in FY2025 from $12.82 in FY2022 while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million [F75][F72][X137].
Operating margin was 34.8% in FY2025, above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [F35][D663][D662].
The FY2025 margin recovered 36.9pp, mostly a 37.7pp swing in other lines as AIPR&D fell away [D452][D468].
Cost of sales held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 on a lower overall royalty rate for CF medicines [D425][P4].
SG&A took 1.3pp off margin as it grew 19.7% against revenue growth of 8.9% [D467][D456][D446].
The FY2024 net margin of -4.9% diverged from operating margin because the 315.5% effective tax rate reflected non-deductible AIPR&D [F54][D390][P5].
Operating cash flow was $3,631.4 million and free cash flow $3,193.8 million in FY2025, a 26.6% free-cash-flow margin [F85][F105][D431].
Free cash flow covered net income 0.81x, below the 1.07x window median and the 1.11x peer median [D435][D675][D694].
Operating cash flow was primarily due to income from operations of $4.2 billion [P1].
Capex rose 47.0% to $437.6 million, 2.09x D&A and 3.6% of revenue [D447][F95][D436][D430].
Cash and investments were $12,320.4 million in FY2025 with no debt, equal to 102.7% of revenue [D438][D13][D440].
That net cash position sits at the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers, whose median is -50.7% of revenue [D691][D692].
Cash rose in FY2025 primarily due to increased cash and marketable securities from product revenue [P2].
Buybacks of $2,017.4 million absorbed 63.2% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was unchanged [D441][D442][D459].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days to 373 in FY2025, the highest in the window [D444][D397].
Inventory of $1,686.8 million now covers a full year of cost of sales, a build that would matter if TRIKAFTA volumes stall [X178][X30].
The effective tax rate moved -300.7pp in FY2025 from the FY2024 level of 315.5%, so the swing is largely base effect [D433][D390][P5].
FY2019 share repurchases were later restated from the $192.0 million first reported; the pack uses the first-reported figure [X141].
If TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth stays below the 0.7pp contribution of FY2025, total growth depends on ALYFTREK holding its 7.6pp [D531][D590].
Free cash flow conversion below the 1.07x window median would confirm the working-capital drag visible in 373 inventory days [D675][D444].
Operating margin falling back toward the 31.8% median would reverse the FY2025 recovery, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D663][F35].
